findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator uses numeric key handling for a datetime ordering
findings.body: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key does int(math.floor(value)) on getattr(item, self.key) and value_from_cursor returns cursor.value unchanged. The only caller, OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint, orders by '-datetime', so value is a datetime: math.floor(datetime) raises TypeError when build_cursor computes next/prev cursors, making the optimized path return 500 on any non-empty page. Even if it did not crash, value_from_cursor would pass a raw integer timestamp into build_queryset's datetime comparison instead of converting it with DateTimePaginator's multiplier/fromtimestamp logic, producing wrong filtering. The paginator should reuse DateTimePaginator's key conversion or the endpoint should not use it for -datetime.

findings.title: Negative-offset queryset slicing raises AssertionError, not graceful pagination
findings.body: When enable_advanced_features is true and a user supplies a cursor with a negative offset (Cursor.from_string accepts e.g. '0:-100:0'), this branch does queryset[start_offset:stop] with start_offset<0. Django QuerySets explicitly raise AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported, contrary to the comment claiming the ORM handles it automatically. Any superuser/global-access user can craft ?optimized_pagination=true&cursor=... to reliably 500 the audit-log endpoint, and stop can also become <=0 giving meaningless slices. Negative offsets must be rejected/clamped with BadPaginationError as OffsetPaginator/ChainPaginator do.

findings.title: BasePaginator change still allows negative offsets for prev cursors on all endpoints
findings.body: The shared BasePaginator.get_result now clamps negative offsets only when not cursor.is_prev; for is_prev cursors it passes the raw user-controlled offset to queryset[start_offset:stop]. Since every DateTimePaginator/Paginator endpoint parses cursors from the query string without rejecting negative offsets, a crafted prev cursor (e.g. value:-5:1) reaches a negative Django queryset slice and raises AssertionError/500. This expands the crash beyond the gated audit-log path to all BasePaginator users, instead of validating offset<0 once in get_result/Cursor.from_string.

findings.title: No tests for optimized pagination branch or negative/malformed cursors
findings.body: The PR adds a new query-param/gating branch (optimized_pagination=true plus is_superuser/has_global_access) and a whole new paginator class, but adds no tests. Existing audit-log tests only exercise DateTimePaginator, so the datetime-key crash and negative-offset crash above are not caught, nor is the authorization gate (non-privileged users must stay on the old paginator, privileged users must get identical rows/cursors). Tests should cover first/next/prev pages via the optimized path, equivalence with DateTimePaginator results, negative-offset cursors, and the gate on/off.
